groups.description: The company this domain is modeled on: PastBook (Amsterdam, founded 2012 in the Rockstart Accelerator), backed by Vortex Capital Partners since December 2015.

links.title: PastBook — Your Memories, Turned into Beautiful Photo Books in Seconds
links.relevance: The company's own proposition: a photo book made in seconds without design work, with 24/7 support via WhatsApp, e-mail and chat — the framing behind every consumer persona.

links.title: PastBook — Vortex Capital Partners investment page
links.relevance: The investor's description: tech-enabled, high growth, growth capital, production facilities on four continents and shipping to more than 150 countries.

links.title: PastBook raises USD 2 million to scale up its one-click photo books platform (Business Wire, 21 September 2017)
links.relevance: The Vortex-led convertible note and follow-on that took total funding above USD 2.5 million, with the founder's eBay background and the one-click positioning.

links.title: Amsterdam's PastBook raises funding led by Vortex (Tech.eu, 21 September 2017)
links.relevance: Independent coverage with the two facts that shape the growth model: 10x year-on-year revenue growth three years in a row and 80% of customers in the USA.

links.title: PastBook raises EUR 350k seed funding (StartupJuncture, 26 December 2015)
links.relevance: The seed round that started the Vortex relationship and dates the company's early one-click social photo book offer.

links.title: Careers — the PastBook team
links.relevance: About 16 named team members and operations in the Netherlands, United States, Sri Lanka and India that enable 24/7 support — the basis of the modeled organisation.

groups.description: The consumer surfaces and the published rules that the customer personas, streams and pricing bricks are built from.

links.title: PastBook: 1-Click Photo Book app
links.relevance: The iOS and Android app with 1M+ downloads: camera roll import by date, location, album or Yearbook mode, calendars and posters — the family memory keeper's primary product.

links.title: Facebook Photo Books — one book per year
links.relevance: The web flow that turns Facebook albums, timeline pictures, cover and profile photos and mobile uploads into one book per year from 2009 to 2025 — the archivist's job in one page.

links.title: Year in Review photo book
links.relevance: The seasonal yearbook product from phone or Facebook and the 10M+ books-created claim that anchor the Q4 campaign and the gift giver persona.

links.title: Pricing and shipping
links.relevance: The price ladder in seven currencies, extra-page prices and the per-country delivery windows that define the commerce and fulfilment KPIs.

links.title: Instagram ends support for photo products
links.relevance: PastBook's own account of losing the Instagram source and redirecting customers to Facebook, the app and manual upload — the case study for platform dependence.

links.title: Sustainability
links.relevance: FSC-certified paper, production in the country of the order, reforestation with Land Life Company and supplier commitments — the claims the partner network must evidence.

links.title: Help center — How much does a Photo Book cost
links.relevance: The cover rules by page count (softcover up to 16 pages, choice at 18 to 26, hardcover 27 to 300, softcover above 300) encoded in the pricing brick.

links.title: Help center — How much does shipping cost
links.relevance: The shipping-cost rules customers and support agents work from when an order spans products or countries.

groups.description: Growth, leadership and product milestones as reported by the company and the press.

links.title: PastBook newsroom
links.relevance: The mission statement, Deloitte Fast50 and FT1000 listings, App Store featuring, highlight video sharing and gift-guide placements in one place.

links.title: PastBook wins the Deloitte Technology Fast50 2019 for Media & Entertainment (Business Wire, 13 October 2019)
links.relevance: The 4,623% turnover growth and top-three overall placement that document the step-change growth the operations model must absorb.

links.title: Fastest growing companies in the Netherlands for the 3rd year in a row
links.relevance: The Fast50 2021 placement with 528% growth, confirming sustained growth after the 2020 leadership change.

links.title: PastBook launches AI-driven app following exponential growth (London Loves Tech, 6 July 2021)
links.relevance: The USD 14.3M 2019 revenue, the projected tripling in 2020, the patent-pending under-60-seconds curation and the market ranking North America, Australia, Europe, UK.

links.title: PastBook announces Wouter Staatsen as CEO and Stefano Cutello as Chief Product & Innovation Officer
links.relevance: The 23 April 2020 leadership change bringing Albelli and Cimpress experience into the company, which shapes the operating model in this domain.

links.title: PastBook appoints Wouter Staatsen as CEO (The Dead Pixels Society)
links.relevance: Photo-industry trade coverage of the same appointment, including the CMO's Albelli background.

groups.description: Where consumers find, rate and complain about the product — the surfaces the growth and support teams manage every day.

links.title: PastBook: 1-Click Photo Book on the App Store
links.relevance: The iOS listing that carries App Store featuring, ratings and privacy labels — a channel partner surface and the top of the install-to-order funnel.

links.title: PastBook on Google Play
links.relevance: The Android listing with its review, rating and policy obligations mirrored from the iOS side.

links.title: PastBook reviews on Trustpilot
links.relevance: TrustScore 4.5 from 35,837 reviews, the reply-to-every-negative-review-within-48-hours commitment and the recurring complaint themes that drive the reprint root-cause model.

groups.description: Market sizing and the incumbents, AI-first peers and platform-native offers that PastBook competes with.

links.title: Europe photobook and album market (Fortune Business Insights)
links.relevance: Sizes Europe at USD 1.05 billion in 2025, 29.96% of the global market — the market context for a company whose customers are mostly outside Europe.

links.title: The photobook market 2025: those who don't scale lose (Beyond Print)
links.relevance: Trade analysis of consolidation and scale economics in photo printing that frames the partner-network versus own-factory choice.

links.title: CEWE achieves all targets in 2025 (EQS News, 26 March 2026)
links.relevance: Europe's photobook leader: EUR 864.5M turnover and a record 6.32 million CEWE PHOTOBOOK copies in 2025 — the scale benchmark for price, quality and delivery.

links.title: Storio group — about us
links.relevance: The Amsterdam neighbour formerly albelli-Photobox Group: six brands, thirteen European markets, over eleven million customers and its own manufacturing sites.

links.title: Scaling revenue with AI (Popsa)
links.relevance: The closest AI-first peer: USD 1M revenue per employee, 46 people, 2 million customers and AI applied across marketing, support and logistics.

links.title: Mixbook — photo books with Mixbook Studio
links.relevance: A US design-led competitor with 6 million+ customers, books up to 400 pages and the Mixbook Studio AI design tool that contests the automated-design claim.

links.title: Order a photo book from Google Photos
links.relevance: The platform-native alternative: softcover and hardcover books of 20 to 140 pages ordered inside the photo library in the US, Canada and 28+ European countries.
